cards.explanation: The answer is rain and dew. Moses, Israel's leader, says, "Let my teaching fall like rain and my speech settle like dew…" (Deuteronomy 32:2). He adds that it's like "…gentle rain on new grass…" Nothing loud or pushy about it. I wish my alarm clock had that kind of manners.

The answer is Rock. Moses sings, "He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just." (Deuteronomy 32:4). A rock holds still when everything else is shaking. I like a name like that, friends, because it tells me where to stand.

The answer is that the LORD is their Father and Creator. Moses asks, "Is He not your Father and Creator? Has He not made you and established you?" (Deuteronomy 32:6). Two big titles in one breath. He's asking whether this is how you repay the One who made you.

The answer is True. Moses sings, "But the LORD’s portion is His people, Jacob His allotted inheritance." (Deuteronomy 32:9). Out of everything the Most High could have called His own, the song names His people. That's a good line to hear.

The answer is in a howling wilderness. Moses sings, "He found him in a desert land, in a barren, howling wilderness…" (Deuteronomy 32:10). Barren and howling, and still the LORD found him there. The song says the LORD surrounded him, instructed him and guarded him.

The answer is wings. Moses sings, "As an eagle stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, He spread His wings to catch them and carried them on His pinions." (Deuteronomy 32:11). Catch them, then carry them. That's a lot of care packed into one picture.

The answer is False. Moses sings, "The LORD alone led him, and no foreign god was with him." (Deuteronomy 32:12). No foreign god was there, let alone helping. I've seen a whole kitchen crowd at one batch, and this is nothing like that. The LORD led His people by Himself.

The answer is False, because the song doesn't call it plain. Moses sings of "…the choicest grains of wheat." and says, "From the juice of the finest grapes you drank the wine." (Deuteronomy 32:14). That's the good stuff, the choicest and the finest. It makes my best cookie dough look humble.

The answer is abandoned. The song says, "He abandoned the God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation." (Deuteronomy 32:15). Just before that, Jeshurun is "…fat, bloated, and gorged." You know that feeling after a whole tray of cookies, when all you want is a nap? Jeshurun got that full, and instead of a nap, he walked out on God.

The answer is demons. Moses sings, "They sacrificed to demons, not to God, to gods they had not known…" (Deuteronomy 32:17). Gods they had not known. They gave their offerings to those instead of to God. That's a heavy part of the song.

The answer is False. Moses sings about "…gods they had not known, to newly arrived gods, which your fathers did not fear." (Deuteronomy 32:17). New arrivals, not old gods. Even the fathers hadn't feared them.

The answer is His own sons and daughters. The song says, "When the LORD saw this, He rejected them, provoked to anger by His sons and daughters." (Deuteronomy 32:19). It's His own people who provoked Him. I think that hurts more than a stranger doing it.

The answer is True. God says, "I will hide My face from them; I will see what will be their end." (Deuteronomy 32:20). He goes on, "For they are a perverse generation…" I think this one hurts to hear. It's a heavy line.

The answer is by those who aren't even a people. God says, "So I will make them jealous by those who are not a people; I will make them angry by a nation without understanding." (Deuteronomy 32:21). Look at how the verse is built. They provoked Him with "…that which is not God…" and the reply comes through "…those who are not a people…" The two halves match.

The answer is that their enemies would take the credit. God says He would have gone further "…if I had not dreaded the taunt of the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand and say: ‘Our own hand has prevailed; it was not the LORD who did all this.’…" (Deuteronomy 32:27). It's about what the enemies would say. They'd take the credit that belongs to Him.

The answer is that the LORD had given them up. Moses asks, "How could one man pursue a thousand, or two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?" (Deuteronomy 32:30). Those numbers don't happen on their own. According to the song, that's the only way it could.

The answer is poisonous. The song says, "Their grapes are poisonous; their clusters are bitter." (Deuteronomy 32:32). The vine is from Sodom and Gomorrah, and the fruit matches. You wouldn't want a taste of that.
The answer is False. God says, "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay." (Deuteronomy 32:35). It belongs to Him, not to His people. That's the statement the song makes.

The answer is when He sees their strength is gone. The song says the LORD "…will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants when He sees that their strength is gone and no one remains, slave or free." (Deuteronomy 32:36). It comes when their strength is gone. The song turns toward hope here.
The answer is True. God says, "See now that I am He; there is no God besides Me." (Deuteronomy 32:39). There is no other. That settles every question.

The answer is no one. God says, "I bring death and I give life; I wound and I heal, and there is no one who can deliver from My hand." (Deuteronomy 32:39). No one at all. Death and life, wounding and healing, and nobody who can pull anyone out of His hand.

The answer is that He lives forever. God says, "For I lift up My hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever…" (Deuteronomy 32:40). His promise is as sure as His own life. It can't get more solid than that.

The answer is nations. Moses sings, "Rejoice, O nations, with His people…" (Deuteronomy 32:43). The call goes out beyond Israel. A song that began by calling the heavens and the earth to listen ends by calling the nations to rejoice.
